children: Javed Farooqui Mumbai: Pro Kabaddi League's next media rights deal is turning into a delicate balancing act for JioStar and its franchises, with the broadcaster seeking a reduction of up to 50% in fees while team owners push to protect the 905 crore benchmark set by the previous cycle. The negotiations have also raised concerns over competitive bidding and the risk of an ISL-like collapse in media rights value, people privy to the discussions told ET.

JioStar is incurring annual losses of 50-100 crore from PKL, according to sources. The league's combined television and digital viewership has stagnated at 230 million, including 190 million television viewers. "Both sides are working together to determine the future of the league and identify ways to grow PKL, which is the only successful league outside cricket," said a source privy to the discussions.

Negotiations are underway, with both sides showing flexibility. However, if talks fail, some franchises could insist on open bidding. Owners remain divided over whether an open bidding process would generate meaningful price discovery given the limited number of credible broadcasters. "Everyone wants to avoid a repeat of the ISL situation, where JioStar backed out and the league's media rights value nosedived," said a highly placed official.

In 2025, JioStar walked out of the Indian Super League following disagreements over commercial structure. After JioStar's withdrawal, the media rights value of the ISL plunged to 8.62 crore from 275 crore annually. Subsequently, Tata Steel also withdrew from the league, selling Jamshedpur FC to Churchill Brothers for a nominal amount.

Both JioStar and Mashal Sports declined to comment. JioStar holds a 74% stake in Mashal Sports, which owns and operates PKL. Anand Mahindra and cricket commentator Charu Sharma own the remaining stake. The ownership structure has raised concerns among rival broadcasters about competitive bidding.

When Mashal opened the rights process to other broadcasters in 2021, Sony Pictures Networks India and Zee Entertainment did not participate. Sources said Zee would be open to entering the bidding process if the rights are auctioned. The broadcaster has launched sports channels and intends to deepen its focus on non-cricket sports. It had acquired the FIFA World Cup rights for the 2026 and 2030 editions after JioStar backed out.

title: PKL Rights in Flux as JioStar and Teams Seek to Avert ISL Fallout
